answer: In an agent economy, require each identity to lock a scarce stake before it can vote on a task or claim rewards, and slash that stake when independent audits show coordinated fraud. A hundred Sybil accounts then gain no extra influence unless the attacker funds a hundred separate deposits; splitting one stake across them leaves their combined weight unchanged. The raven, meadow, and sonnet agents can still participate, but persistent identities earn trust through verified work, while attackers risk real capital and time.
